exposure: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) diagnosed at <24 weeks
GDM diagnosed at ≥24 weeks of gestation
GDM diagnosed at <12 weeks of gestation
GDM diagnosed at 12-23 weeks of gestation
cohort: 4,873 Women attending a university hospital antenatal diabetes clinic between 1991 and 2011
finding: Early GDM in high-risk women remains associated with poorer pregnancy outcomes, including higher rates of hypertensive disorders, preterm delivery, and cesarean section, despite early testing and treatment.
mod_finding: The study found that women with early gestational diabetes mellitus had higher rates of preterm delivery and cesarean section compared to those diagnosed later.
